stories.headline: Orpo drone-readiness interview triggers political firestorm over civilian responsibility
stories.summary: Prime Minister Orpo's Helsingin Sanomat interview arguing that Finnish citizens lack personal resilience for emergencies sparked a week-long political controversy. Opposition parties accused Orpo of shifting blame for governmental failures in the drone incident response onto citizens; Orpo denied this, insisting he was misunderstood. The parliamentary defence committee separately demanded rapid deployment of the delayed cell-broadcast emergency alert system.

stories.headline: SDP re-elects Lindtman at Tampere congress, picks new deputy leadership ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: The Social Democratic Party held its three-day congress in Tampere, re-electing Antti Lindtman as leader without opposition and selecting three female deputy leaders: Nasima Razmyar, Niina Malm, and 29-year-old newcomer Pinja Perholehto. The congress also committed to the debt-brake framework while debating fiscal policy, labour rights, immigration, and the party's readiness for government.

stories.headline: Stubb named in diplomatic circles as candidate for Europe-Russia peace negotiator role
stories.summary: Helsingin Sanomat reported, citing ten diplomatic sources across multiple European countries, that President Stubb's name is prominent in speculation about who could represent Europe in eventual peace talks between Ukraine and Russia. Sources described Stubb as having strong relationships with both President Zelenskyy and President Trump, and indicated Stubb himself wants the role.

stories.headline: Stubb addresses Ukraine war, Gaza flotilla, and drone communications in Yle Radio Q&A
stories.summary: President Stubb participated in a live public Q&A on Yle Radio Suomi on 24 May, covering a range of topics: he said Ukraine is now in its strongest position, called for improved official communications on future drone incidents, condemned Israel's national security minister for humiliating Gaza aid flotilla activists, and commented on Russia's overnight missile strike on Kyiv.

stories.headline: Orpo meets Modi at Nordic-India Oslo summit; Finland to host next summit around 2028
stories.summary: Prime Minister Orpo represented Finland at the Nordic-India summit in Oslo on 19 May, holding a bilateral meeting with Indian PM Modi. The parties agreed to aim for more than doubling Finland-India trade by 2030, with cooperation areas including AI, clean energy, and space technology. Finland was selected to host the next Nordic-India summit, planned for around 2028. Coverage also noted a controversy over a Norwegian journalist's exchange with Modi's delegation.

stories.headline: Finland announces it will exceed NATO's 1.5% defence-and-security spending target in 2026
stories.summary: Defence Minister Häkkänen announced that Finland will exceed NATO's 1.5% of GDP target for defence- and security-related spending in 2026, the first year it is formally reportable. The announcement covers civil resilience, readiness duties, and capabilities alongside hard defence spending. Finland separately committed to raising core defence spending to 3.2% of GDP by 2029.
